title: Resident Evil
review: The second time around it felt more like a comedy, and less like a horror. The lack of suspense from watching a horror movie twice in a short period, allowed the rest to shine. It's gloriously gory, and many of the laughs come from unexpectedly over-the-top deaths. I won't say it's perfectly grotesque, as none of the injuries are remotely believable or realistic. I find Austin Abrhams' protagonist charming in a way, while all the minor characters are weaker and less serious. It's almost like watching a real human get stuck in a video game world, and there are no other real people there, only video game NPCs. They're written more like NPCs too.
